text.p: Manufacturing group Hawker Richardson Ltd said on Wednesday it recommended that shareholders reject the A$1.60 per share takeover bid by investment group Austrim Ltd.
"The company is at an exciting stage of its development with plans for rapid growth and a talented management team capable of achieving them," Hawker directors said.
"The market accepts this and clearly believes the company is worth more than A$1.60 per share."
Directors said they would not accept the offer for their own shares.
Hawker shares were five cents lower at A$1.75 at 2.20 p.m. (0420 GMT). The Austrim bid values Hawker, which makes car components and other engineering products, at A$58.31 million.
Hawker has 36.45 million shares on issue.

Hawker managing director Graeme Salthouse said the Austrim bid is opportunistic and has been carefully timed to take place just as benefits start to emerge and before recent acquisitions can be reported and assessed by the market.
Salthouse said Austrim chief executive Alan Jackson, the former head of the BTR group in Australia and the United Kingdom, cannot expect to buy the company at such a low price.
He also said he noted that Austrim did not intend to increase its offer at this stage.
